# 1. Load Curation File and Build Leading-Edge Gene Table

```{r load_curation_file}
# Load the a priori curated GO term file. Sheet names correspond to the
# three contrasts. Column header rows differ between sheets (some sheets
# have a "Parameters:" note row above the real header), hence the
# different `skip` values — confirmed by inspecting each sheet directly.

curation_eMPC_vs_iPSC <- read_excel(
  "~/Desktop/Tese/R/GSEA_GO_BP_curated_apriori.xlsx", sheet = "eMPC_vs_iPSC", skip = 2)
curation_EC_vs_eMPC   <- read_excel(
  "~/Desktop/Tese/R/GSEA_GO_BP_curated_apriori.xlsx", sheet = "EC_vs_eMPC", skip = 0)
curation_EC_vs_iPSC   <- read_excel(
  "~/Desktop/Tese/R/GSEA_GO_BP_curated_apriori.xlsx", sheet = "EC_vs_iPSC", skip = 0)

cat("Columns:", paste(colnames(curation_eMPC_vs_iPSC), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r extract_leading_edge}
# Extract leading edge genes from pathways marked "yes_apriori" in the
# a priori curation. Returns one row per (pathway, gene) pair, with
# contrast_side, biological_category, and NES carried along.
#
# Columns are renamed by position using base R (not tidyselect helpers
# like all_of()/.data[[]]) — some column names in the curated file carry
# hidden characters (e.g. \r\n) that caused unpredictable failures with
# tidyselect indirection. All dplyr/tidyr calls are namespaced (dplyr::,
# tidyr::) because another loaded package was silently masking
# dplyr::rename()/dplyr::filter() in this session.

extract_leadinggene <- function(curation_df, contrast_name) {

  # Column order in GSEA_GO_BP_curated_apriori.xlsx:
  # 1 = Include in signature? (old, data-driven — not used here)
  # 2 = include_apriori (new, a priori selection — used here)
  # 3 = Stage-associated side of contrast
  # 4 = Biological category
  # last = leadingEdge
  n <- ncol(curation_df)
  colnames(curation_df)[2] <- "include_apriori_std"
  colnames(curation_df)[3] <- "contrast_side_std"
  colnames(curation_df)[4] <- "biological_category_std"
  colnames(curation_df)[n] <- "leadingEdge_std"

  # Stop loudly if the columns aren't what we expect, instead of
  # silently extracting from the wrong columns
  stopifnot(colnames(curation_df)[2] == "include_apriori_std")

  selected <- curation_df[
    !is.na(curation_df$include_apriori_std) &
    curation_df$include_apriori_std == "yes_apriori", ]

  cat(contrast_name, "— yes_apriori pathways:", nrow(selected), "\n")

  result <- selected %>%
    dplyr::select(
      pathway              = pathway,
      pathway_clean         = pathway_clean,
      contrast_side         = contrast_side_std,
      biological_category   = biological_category_std,
      NES,
      leadingEdge           = leadingEdge_std
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      contrast = contrast_name,
      leadingEdge = as.character(leadingEdge)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::separate_rows(leadingEdge, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
    dplyr::rename(gene = leadingEdge) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(gene), gene != "")

  return(result)
}

le_eMPC_vs_iPSC <- extract_leadinggene(curation_eMPC_vs_iPSC, "eMPC_vs_iPSC")
le_EC_vs_eMPC   <- extract_leadinggene(curation_EC_vs_eMPC,   "EC_vs_eMPC")
le_EC_vs_iPSC   <- extract_leadinggene(curation_EC_vs_iPSC,   "EC_vs_iPSC")

le_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(le_eMPC_vs_iPSC, le_EC_vs_eMPC, le_EC_vs_iPSC)

cat("\nTotal gene-pathway associations extracted:", nrow(le_all), "\n")
```

# 2. Build Wide-Format logFC/t/padj Table (L1, L2, L3)

```{r load_toptable_wide}
# Load the full topTable (all genes tested, not just DEGs) for the three
# contrasts, and reshape into a single wide table: one row per gene, with
# logFC, t-statistic, and adjusted p-value for each contrast side by side.
#
# L1 = eMPC - iPSC  (mesoderm induction step)
# L2 = EC   - eMPC  (endothelial specification step)
# L3 = EC   - iPSC  (full trajectory, cumulative)
#
# L1 and L2 are the two legs used to classify each gene's trajectory
# shape below. L3 is kept for QC and as a measure of overall change
# and statistical evidence across the full trajectory.

d1 <- read_excel("DEGs_full_toptable_three_contrasts.xlsx", sheet = "eMPC_vs_iPSC") %>%
  dplyr::rename(L1_logFC = logFC, L1_t = t, L1_pval = P.Value, L1_padj = adj.P.Val)

d2 <- read_excel("DEGs_full_toptable_three_contrasts.xlsx", sheet = "EC_vs_eMPC") %>%
  dplyr::rename(L2_logFC = logFC, L2_t = t, L2_pval = P.Value, L2_padj = adj.P.Val)

d3 <- read_excel("DEGs_full_toptable_three_contrasts.xlsx", sheet = "EC_vs_iPSC") %>%
  dplyr::rename(L3_logFC = logFC, L3_t = t, L3_pval = P.Value, L3_padj = adj.P.Val)

wide <- d1 %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(d2, by = "GeneID") %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(d3, by = "GeneID")

cat("Genes in wide table:", nrow(wide), "\n")
```

# 3. QC - Confirm L3 ≈ L1 + L2

```{r qc_l3}
# L3 (EC vs iPSC) should equal L1 + L2 almost exactly, because all three
# contrasts were extracted via contrasts.fit() from the same lmFit object
# (same design matrix, same array weights). This is an algebraic identity
# of the model coefficients, not a biological result — a large deviation
# here would point to a gene mapping problem, duplicated rows, or a
# contrast built from a different fit, and should be investigated before
# trusting anything downstream.

wide <- wide %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    L3_predicted = L1_logFC + L2_logFC,
    L3_diff      = L3_logFC - L3_predicted
  )

cat("=== QC: L3 vs L1+L2 ===\n")
cat("Max absolute deviation:", max(abs(wide$L3_diff)), "\n")
print(summary(wide$L3_diff))

# Flag any gene with a deviation above floating-point noise (should be none)
qc_flag <- wide %>% dplyr::filter(abs(L3_diff) > 1e-6)
cat("\nGenes with L3 deviation > 1e-6:", nrow(qc_flag), "\n")
if (nrow(qc_flag) > 0) print(qc_flag$GeneID)
```

# 4. Restrict to Module-Associated Genes

```{r filter_module_genes}
# Restrict the wide table to the genes already identified as leading-edge
# members of at least one yes_apriori pathway (le_all, built in Section 1).
# This is the full module-associated gene set (856 genes) — the official
# molecular signature. No reduction to "core genes" happens at this stage.

module_genes <- unique(le_all$gene)
cat("Module genes (from le_all):", length(module_genes), "\n")

wide_modules <- wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(GeneID %in% module_genes) %>%
  dplyr::select(GeneID, L1_logFC, L1_t, L1_padj,
                        L2_logFC, L2_t, L2_padj,
                        L3_logFC, L3_t, L3_padj)

cat("Module genes matched in topTable:", nrow(wide_modules), "\n")
cat("Module genes NOT found in topTable:", length(module_genes) - nrow(wide_modules), "\n")
```

# 5. Classify Gene Trajectories (trajectory_sign_class)

```{r trajectory_sign_class}
# Classify each gene by the sign of L1 and L2 only — four possible
# combinations, no magnitude threshold applied at this stage. This is a
# deliberately conservative first pass: sign alone already separates
# genuinely different biological stories (transient peak/trough at the
# eMPC stage vs. progressive monotonic change across the full
# trajectory), and applying a magnitude cutoff before inspecting the
# real distribution would risk imposing an arbitrary boundary the data
# may not support.

wide_modules <- wide_modules %>%
  dplyr::mutate(trajectory_sign_class = dplyr::case_when(
    L1_logFC > 0 & L2_logFC > 0 ~ "monotonic_increase",
    L1_logFC < 0 & L2_logFC < 0 ~ "monotonic_decrease",
    L1_logFC > 0 & L2_logFC < 0 ~ "eMPC_peak",
    L1_logFC < 0 & L2_logFC > 0 ~ "eMPC_trough",
    TRUE ~ "other_zero"
  ))

cat("=== trajectory_sign_class distribution ===\n")
print(table(wide_modules$trajectory_sign_class))
print(round(prop.table(table(wide_modules$trajectory_sign_class)), 3))
```

# 6. Flag Weak/Near-Flat Transitions

```{r near_flat_flag}
# Flag genes where at least one leg (L1 or L2) is both small in magnitude
# (|logFC| < 0.5) AND not statistically significant (padj >= 0.05).
#
# This does NOT reclassify the gene or remove it from its
# trajectory_sign_class — it only marks that one of the two legs behind
# that label is effectively flat, so the "monotonic" or "peak/trough"
# story should not be over-interpreted for that specific gene when
# writing up individual examples.

wide_modules <- wide_modules %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    L1_weak = abs(L1_logFC) < 0.5 & L1_padj >= 0.05,
    L2_weak = abs(L2_logFC) < 0.5 & L2_padj >= 0.05,
    near_flat_transition = L1_weak | L2_weak
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-L1_weak, -L2_weak)

cat("Genes with near_flat_transition = TRUE:",
    sum(wide_modules$near_flat_transition),
    sprintf("(%.0f%%)\n", 100 * mean(wide_modules$near_flat_transition)))

cat("\nBy class:\n")
wide_modules %>%
  dplyr::group_by(trajectory_sign_class) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), n_near_flat = sum(near_flat_transition), .groups = "drop")
```

# 7. Export Gene Trajectory Table

```{r export_gene_trajectory}
# Export the final gene-level trajectory table: 856 module-associated
# genes, with L1/L2/L3 (logFC, t, padj) and the trajectory_sign_class /
# near_flat_transition annotations. This is the input for the next stage
# (biological_module annotation and heatmap construction).

write_xlsx(
  list("gene_trajectory" = wide_modules),
  path = "gene_trajectory_L1L2L3.xlsx"
)

cat("Exported gene_trajectory_L1L2L3.xlsx —", nrow(wide_modules), "genes\n")
```

# 8. Attach Biological Module Annotation

```{r attach_biological_module}
# For each gene, summarise which biological_category (module) and which
# pathway(s) it comes from, across all yes_apriori pathways it appears in
# as a leading-edge member. A gene can belong to more than one module —
# this is captured as a semicolon-separated list, not collapsed into a
# single "primary module" here. That reduction (if needed for heatmap
# row_split) is a separate, later decision — see Section 9.

gene_module_summary <- le_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gene) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    biological_modules = paste(sort(unique(biological_category)), collapse = "; "),
    n_modules           = dplyr::n_distinct(biological_category),
    source_pathways      = paste(sort(unique(pathway_clean)), collapse = "; "),
    n_pathways           = dplyr::n_distinct(pathway),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("Genes summarised:", nrow(gene_module_summary), "\n")
cat("Genes belonging to more than one module:",
    sum(gene_module_summary$n_modules > 1),
    sprintf("(%.0f%%)\n", 100 * mean(gene_module_summary$n_modules > 1)))
```

```{r join_module_to_trajectory}
# Join the module annotation onto the gene trajectory table (one row per
# gene, matching the 856 already confirmed in Section 4/7).

gene_trajectory_annotated <- wide_modules %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_module_summary, by = c("GeneID" = "gene"))

cat("Rows after join:", nrow(gene_trajectory_annotated), "\n")
cat("Rows with missing module annotation (should be 0):",
    sum(is.na(gene_trajectory_annotated$biological_modules)), "\n")
```

```{r export_annotated}
write_xlsx(
  list("gene_trajectory_annotated" = gene_trajectory_annotated),
  path = "gene_trajectory_annotated.xlsx"
)

cat("Exported gene_trajectory_annotated.xlsx —", nrow(gene_trajectory_annotated), "genes\n")
```

# 9. Signature Heatmap — 856 Genes × 9 Samples

```{r load_y_and_annotations}
# Load the voom-normalized expression matrix (y$E) from the backbone
# pipeline, and the gene-level annotation table built in Sections 1-8
# (biological module membership, trajectory class).

library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(grid)

y <- readRDS("y_voom_backbone.rds")

cat("Genes in y$E:", nrow(y$E), "| Samples:", ncol(y$E), "\n")
```

```{r determine_dominant_module}
# For row_split purposes only (figure layout), assign each gene a single
# "dominant" module — the biological_category in which it appears as a
# leading-edge member in the most distinct yes_apriori pathways. This is
# NOT a claim of exclusive biological membership: genes belonging to more
# than one module keep their full membership list in the side annotation
# panel built below. The dominant module only determines which block of
# the heatmap the gene's row is drawn in.

module_pathway_counts <- le_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gene, biological_category) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_pathways_in_module = dplyr::n_distinct(pathway), .groups = "drop")

dominant_module <- module_pathway_counts %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gene) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(n_pathways_in_module, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, dominant_module = biological_category)

cat("Genes with dominant module assigned:", nrow(dominant_module), "\n")
```

```{r build_expression_matrix}
# Subset y$E to the 856 module-associated genes, in the order defined by
# gene_trajectory_annotated. Genes not present in y$E (e.g. removed by
# low-expression filtering upstream) are reported and dropped.

genes_use <- gene_trajectory_annotated$GeneID
genes_use_present <- genes_use[genes_use %in% rownames(y$E)]

cat("Module genes requested:", length(genes_use), "\n")
cat("Module genes found in y$E:", length(genes_use_present), "\n")
cat("Module genes missing from y$E (filtered out upstream):",
    length(genes_use) - length(genes_use_present), "\n")

mat <- y$E[genes_use_present, , drop = FALSE]

# Row z-score (per gene), same convention as the canonical marker heatmap
mat_z <- t(scale(t(mat)))
mat_z[is.na(mat_z)] <- 0

# Clean column names to match the canonical marker heatmap convention
colnames(mat_z) <- c(
  "iPSC_1", "iPSC_2", "iPSC_3",
  "eMPC_1", "eMPC_2", "eMPC_3",
  "EC_1", "EC_2", "EC_3"
)
```

```{r build_row_split_and_side_annotation}
# Row split: dominant module (layout only, see note above)
row_split <- factor(
  dominant_module$dominant_module[match(genes_use_present, dominant_module$gene)]
)

# Side annotation: full module membership (not just dominant), one binary
# column per module. This is the honest record of every module a gene
# belongs to — the row_split above only reflects the single strongest one.
all_modules <- sort(unique(le_all$biological_category))

membership_mat <- sapply(all_modules, function(m) {
  genes_in_m <- unique(le_all$gene[le_all$biological_category == m])
  as.integer(genes_use_present %in% genes_in_m)
})
rownames(membership_mat) <- genes_use_present
colnames(membership_mat) <- all_modules

cat("Row split levels:", paste(levels(row_split), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r draw_heatmap_full_supplement, fig.width=14, fig.height=40}
# Supplementary figure: full 856-gene heatmap, all modules, for
# documentation purposes. Not intended as the main results figure —
# see Section 10 (module-score heatmap) for that. Row titles are kept
# small and horizontal to avoid overlap at this many row-split groups.

col_group <- factor(
  c(rep("iPSC", 3), rep("eMPC", 3), rep("EC", 3)),
  levels = c("iPSC", "eMPC", "EC")
)

top_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Group = anno_block(
    gp = gpar(fill = "grey95", col = "grey70"),
    labels = c("iPSC", "eMPC", "EC"),
    labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold", col = "black")
  ),
  show_annotation_name = FALSE,
  height = unit(7, "mm")
)

col_fun <- colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))

ht_main <- Heatmap(
  mat_z,
  name = "z-score",
  col = col_fun,
  column_split = col_group,
  top_annotation = top_ha,
  row_split = row_split,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  cluster_row_slices = FALSE,
  show_row_names = FALSE,
  row_title_rot = 0,
  row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6),
  row_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
  column_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
  border = TRUE
)

ht_membership <- Heatmap(
  membership_mat,
  name = "module\nmembership",
  col = c("0" = "white", "1" = "grey30"),
  show_row_names = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6),
  column_title = "Full module membership",
  column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9),
  width = unit(4, "cm")
)

draw(ht_main + ht_membership,
     heatmap_legend_side = "right",
     annotation_legend_side = "right")
```

# 10. Module-Score Heatmap (Main Figure)

```{r compute_module_scores}
# For each biological module, compute a per-sample score as the mean
# z-score across all genes belonging to that module (based on the full
# membership list from le_all, not the single "dominant module" used
# only for the row_split layout in Section 9). A gene belonging to more
# than one module contributes to the score of each — this is expected
# and not corrected for here; modules that share many genes will show
# correlated scores as a direct consequence.

# mat_z (genes x 9 samples, row z-scored) already exists from Section 9.

module_gene_list <- split(le_all$gene, le_all$biological_category)
module_gene_list <- module_gene_list[names(module_gene_list) != "pluripotency / stem cell maintenance"]
module_gene_list <- lapply(module_gene_list, function(g) intersect(unique(g), rownames(mat_z)))

module_score_mat <- t(sapply(module_gene_list, function(genes) {
  colMeans(mat_z[genes, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
}))

cat("Modules:", nrow(module_score_mat), "| Samples:", ncol(module_score_mat), "\n")
cat("Genes per module (range):", paste(range(sapply(module_gene_list, length)), collapse = "-"), "\n")
```

```{r draw_module_score_heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Display names (American spelling, sentence case) and fixed module order,
# identical to the a priori GO BP matrix figure (Section 4.5.1) and Section 4.6.
# Renaming is applied to a copy (module_score_plot) so that module_score_mat
# keeps the original category names used elsewhere in this Rmd.

module_display_names <- c(
  "mesoderm development"                            = "Mesoderm development",
  "embryonic patterning and morphogenesis"          = "Embryonic patterning and morphogenesis",
  "mesenchymal development"                         = "Mesenchymal development",
  "epithelial-mesenchymal transition"               = "Epithelial\u2013mesenchymal transition",
  "cardiovascular and endocardial development"      = "Cardiovascular and endocardial development",
  "developmental signalling"                        = "Developmental signaling",
  "endothelial specification"                       = "Endothelial specification",
  "VEGF signaling and endothelial response"         = "VEGF signaling and endothelial response",
  "angiogenesis / vasculogenesis"                   = "Angiogenesis / vasculogenesis",
  "cell adhesion and cell-matrix interaction"       = "Cell adhesion and cell\u2013matrix interaction",
  "extracellular matrix organization / remodelling" = "Extracellular matrix organization / remodeling",
  "mechanotransduction / shear stress"              = "Mechanotransduction / shear stress",
  "vascular homeostasis / fluid regulation"         = "Vascular homeostasis / fluid regulation",
  "hemostasis / coagulation"                        = "Hemostasis / coagulation",
  "immune / inflammatory response"                  = "Immune / inflammatory response"
)

module_score_plot <- module_score_mat
raw_names <- trimws(rownames(module_score_plot))

# Check: every module name must have a display name (expect character(0))
print(setdiff(raw_names, names(module_display_names)))

rownames(module_score_plot) <- module_display_names[raw_names]

# Fixed order (same as the names vector above)
module_score_plot <- module_score_plot[unname(module_display_names), , drop = FALSE]

# Check: 15 modules, no missing rows (expect 15 and FALSE)
nrow(module_score_plot)
any(is.na(rownames(module_score_plot)))

col_group <- factor(
  c(rep("iPSC", 3), rep("eMPC", 3), rep("EC", 3)),
  levels = c("iPSC", "eMPC", "EC")
)

top_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Group = anno_block(
    gp = gpar(fill = "grey95", col = "grey70"),
    labels = c("iPSC", "eMPC", "EC"),
    labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold", col = "black")
  ),
  show_annotation_name = FALSE,
  height = unit(7, "mm")
)

col_fun_score <- colorRamp2(
  c(-max(abs(module_score_plot)), 0, max(abs(module_score_plot))),
  c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B")
)

ht_scores <- Heatmap(
  module_score_plot,
  name = "Module\nscore",
  col = col_fun_score,
  column_split = col_group,
  column_title = NULL,
  top_annotation = top_ha,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  row_names_side = "left",
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  row_names_max_width = max_text_width(rownames(module_score_plot),
                                       gp = gpar(fontsize = 10)),
  column_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
  border = TRUE,
  cell_fun = function(j, i, x, y, width, height, fill) {
    grid.text(sprintf("%.2f", module_score_plot[i, j]), x, y,
              gp = gpar(fontsize = 7, col = "black"))
  }
)

draw(ht_scores)
```

```{r export_module_scores}
write_xlsx(
  list("module_scores" = as.data.frame(module_score_mat) %>%
         tibble::rownames_to_column("biological_module")),
  path = "module_scores_by_sample.xlsx"
)

cat("Exported module_scores_by_sample.xlsx —", nrow(module_score_mat), "modules\n")
```

# 11. Core Gene Heatmap (Secondary Figure — Representative Genes per Module)

```{r select_core_genes}
# Select up to 10 representative "core genes" per module, from the full
# leading-edge gene set, using:
#   1. Recurrence — number of distinct yes_apriori pathways within that
#      module in which the gene appears as a leading-edge member
#      (module_pathway_counts, built in Section 9). This criterion only
#      discriminates between genes in modules with more than one pathway.
#   2. Stage-aligned expression — the gene's mean z-score at the stage
#      associated with the module. The module stage is the stage with the
#      highest mean module score (Section 10), so core genes represent the
#      same stage pattern shown in the module-score heatmap.
#   Safeguard: the gene must be significant (padj < 0.05) in at least one
#   of the two contrasts involving the module stage:
#      eMPC modules: L1 (eMPC vs iPSC) or L2 (EC vs eMPC)
#      EC modules:   L2 (EC vs eMPC)  or L3 (EC vs iPSC)
#
# "pluripotency / stem cell maintenance" is excluded, as in Section 10:
# its single GO term is significant only in EC vs eMPC.

n_per_module <- 10

# Sample columns per stage
stage_cols <- list(
  iPSC = grep("^iPSC", colnames(mat_z), value = TRUE),
  eMPC = grep("^eMPC", colnames(mat_z), value = TRUE),
  EC   = grep("^EC",   colnames(mat_z), value = TRUE)
)

# Stage associated with each module (highest mean module score)
module_stage <- tibble::tibble(
  biological_category = trimws(rownames(module_score_mat)),
  iPSC = rowMeans(module_score_mat[, stage_cols$iPSC, drop = FALSE]),
  eMPC = rowMeans(module_score_mat[, stage_cols$eMPC, drop = FALSE]),
  EC   = rowMeans(module_score_mat[, stage_cols$EC,   drop = FALSE])
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    module_stage = c("iPSC", "eMPC", "EC")[max.col(cbind(iPSC, eMPC, EC),
                                                    ties.method = "first")]
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(biological_category, module_stage)

# Check: module stage assignment (expect 5 eMPC and 10 EC, no iPSC)
print(module_stage, n = Inf)
stopifnot(all(module_stage$module_stage %in% c("eMPC", "EC")))

# Mean z-score of each gene at eMPC and at EC
gene_stage_z <- tibble::tibble(
  gene   = rownames(mat_z),
  z_eMPC = rowMeans(mat_z[, stage_cols$eMPC, drop = FALSE]),
  z_EC   = rowMeans(mat_z[, stage_cols$EC,   drop = FALSE])
)

gene_module_scored <- module_pathway_counts %>%
  dplyr::mutate(biological_category = trimws(biological_category)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(biological_category != "pluripotency / stem cell maintenance") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    gene_trajectory_annotated %>%
      dplyr::select(GeneID, L1_logFC, L1_padj, L2_logFC, L2_padj,
                    L3_logFC, L3_padj, trajectory_sign_class, near_flat_transition),
    by = c("gene" = "GeneID")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(L3_logFC)) %>%  # keep only genes present in the trajectory table
  dplyr::left_join(module_stage, by = "biological_category") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_stage_z, by = "gene") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    stage_z = ifelse(module_stage == "eMPC", z_eMPC, z_EC),
    sig_stage_contrast = ifelse(
      module_stage == "eMPC",
      L1_padj < 0.05 | L2_padj < 0.05,
      L2_padj < 0.05 | L3_padj < 0.05
    )
  )

# Check: every module matched a stage (expect 0)
sum(is.na(gene_module_scored$module_stage))

# Previous selection (L3-based tiebreak), kept only for comparison
core_genes_old <- gene_module_scored %>%
  dplyr::group_by(biological_category) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_pathways_in_module), L3_padj,
                 dplyr::desc(abs(L3_logFC)), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = n_per_module) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# New selection
core_genes <- gene_module_scored %>%
  dplyr::filter(sig_stage_contrast) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(biological_category) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_pathways_in_module), dplyr::desc(stage_z),
                 .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = n_per_module) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

cat("Core genes selected:", nrow(core_genes), "across",
    dplyr::n_distinct(core_genes$biological_category), "modules\n")
cat("Unique genes (some may repeat across modules):", dplyr::n_distinct(core_genes$gene), "\n")

# Check: genes per module (expect 10 each; fewer means not enough significant genes)
print(dplyr::count(core_genes, biological_category), n = Inf)

# Check: trajectory classes of core genes per module
print(table(core_genes$biological_category, core_genes$trajectory_sign_class))

# Comparison with the previous selection: genes kept, removed and added per module
selection_changes <- dplyr::full_join(
  core_genes_old %>% dplyr::distinct(biological_category, gene) %>% dplyr::mutate(old = TRUE),
  core_genes     %>% dplyr::distinct(biological_category, gene) %>% dplyr::mutate(new = TRUE),
  by = c("biological_category", "gene")
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    status = dplyr::case_when(
      old & new ~ "kept",
      old       ~ "removed",
      TRUE      ~ "added"
    )
  )

print(table(selection_changes$biological_category, selection_changes$status))
```

```{r build_core_gene_matrix}
# Build the expression matrix for the core gene set. If a gene was
# selected under more than one module, it appears once per module here
# (deliberately — the point of this figure is "which genes represent
# module X", so the same gene can illustrate more than one module).
# Module labels use the display names of the module-score heatmap
# (module_display_names, Section 10): American spelling, sentence case.
# Modules are ordered alphabetically (case-insensitive).
# n_show controls how many core genes per module are displayed in the
# figure (the selection itself and the exported table keep all 10).

n_show <- 10  # set to 5 for the main-text version of the figure

# Wrap long module names for the row titles
module_labels_wrapped <- vapply(module_display_names, function(x)
  paste(strwrap(x, width = 28), collapse = "\n"), character(1))

core_gene_order <- core_genes %>%
  dplyr::group_by(biological_category) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_pathways_in_module), dplyr::desc(stage_z),
                 .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = n_show) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(tolower(biological_category), dplyr::desc(n_pathways_in_module),
                 dplyr::desc(stage_z)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(module_label = unname(module_labels_wrapped[biological_category]))

# Check: every module has a display name (expect 0)
sum(is.na(core_gene_order$module_label))

mat_core <- mat_z[core_gene_order$gene, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(mat_core) <- core_gene_order$gene

row_split_core <- factor(core_gene_order$module_label,
                         levels = unique(core_gene_order$module_label))

cat("Core gene matrix:", nrow(mat_core), "rows x", ncol(mat_core), "columns\n")
```

```{r draw_core_gene_heatmap, fig.width=7, fig.height=2 + nrow(mat_core) * 0.13}
# Figure height scales with the number of displayed genes
# (about 21 in for 150 rows, about 12 in for 75 rows).
# Column width is fixed (8 mm per sample) and thin white lines separate cells.

col_group <- factor(
  c(rep("iPSC", 3), rep("eMPC", 3), rep("EC", 3)),
  levels = c("iPSC", "eMPC", "EC")
)

top_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Group = anno_block(
    gp = gpar(fill = "grey95", col = "grey70"),
    labels = c("iPSC", "eMPC", "EC"),
    labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold", col = "black")
  ),
  show_annotation_name = FALSE,
  height = unit(7, "mm")
)

col_fun <- colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))

ht_core <- Heatmap(
  mat_core,
  name = "z-score",
  col = col_fun,
  width = unit(8 * ncol(mat_core), "mm"),
  rect_gp = gpar(col = "white", lwd = 0.4),
  column_split = col_group,
  column_title = NULL,
  top_annotation = top_ha,
  row_split = row_split_core,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  cluster_row_slices = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7),
  row_title_rot = 0,
  row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8, fontface = "bold"),
  row_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
  column_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
  border = TRUE
)

# Left padding so that long module names are not cut
# (order: bottom, left, top, right)
draw(ht_core, padding = unit(c(2, 12, 2, 2), "mm"))
```

```{r export_core_genes}
# Export the core gene table, including the module stage and the
# stage-aligned z-score used for selection, plus the display module name.

core_genes_export <- core_genes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(module = unname(module_display_names[biological_category])) %>%
  dplyr::select(module, biological_category, gene, n_pathways_in_module,
                module_stage, stage_z, L1_logFC, L1_padj, L2_logFC, L2_padj,
                L3_logFC, L3_padj, trajectory_sign_class, near_flat_transition)

write_xlsx(
  list("core_genes" = core_genes_export,
       "selection_changes" = selection_changes),
  path = "core_genes_by_module.xlsx"
)

cat("Exported core_genes_by_module.xlsx —", nrow(core_genes_export), "rows\n")
```

# 12. Illustrative Expression Trajectory Plots — one representative gene per trajectory_sign_class

```{r select_representative_genes}
# Pick the strongest, cleanest representative per trajectory_sign_class:
# excludes near_flat_transition genes, then ranks by combined significance
# (lowest max of L1_padj, L2_padj) as a simple robustness criterion.

representative_genes <- gene_trajectory_annotated %>%
  dplyr::filter(!near_flat_transition) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(worst_padj = pmax(L1_padj, L2_padj)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(trajectory_sign_class) %>%
  dplyr::slice_min(worst_padj, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

print(representative_genes[, c("GeneID","trajectory_sign_class","L1_logFC","L2_logFC")])
```

```{r trajectory_line_plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
y <- readRDS("y_voom_backbone.rds")

genes_to_plot <- representative_genes$GeneID
expr_long <- as.data.frame(y$E[genes_to_plot, , drop = FALSE]) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-Gene, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Expression") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Stage = dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("iPSC", Sample) ~ "iPSC",
    grepl("eMPC", Sample) ~ "eMPC",
    grepl("EC", Sample)   ~ "EC"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Stage = factor(Stage, levels = c("iPSC","eMPC","EC")))

ggplot(expr_long, aes(x = Stage, y = Expression, group = Sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = Gene), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1, color = "#B2182B") +
  facet_wrap(~ Gene, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Representative genes per trajectory class",
       y = "log2-CPM (voom normalized)", x = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
